Surah Qaf [Meccan, except verse 38, which is Medinan; it has 45 verses]

﴿Qaf﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it. ﴿By the glorious Qur'an﴾, the noble one. (The disbelievers of Mecca did not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ).)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 2:

﴿Nay, but they wonder that there has come to them a warner from among themselves﴾, a messenger from themselves, warning them with the Fire after resurrection. ﴿So the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing"﴾, namely, the warning.

﴿Is it when﴾ (with the two hamzas pronounced clearly, or the second softened, and an alif inserted between them, both readings being permitted) ﴿we have died and become dust﴾ will we return? ﴿That is a far return﴾, extremely distant.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 4:

﴿We have certainly known what the earth diminishes of them﴾ [i.e., what it consumes] ﴿of them, and with Us is a Book preserved﴾ [i.e., the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz)], in which are all things decreed.

Nay, they have denied the truth ﴿bal kadhdhabu bil-haqq﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿lamma ja'ahum﴾ when it came to them. ﴿Fahum﴾, concerning the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, ﴿fi amrin marij﴾ are in a confused, disturbed state. At one time they said he is a sorcerer and it is sorcery; at another time, that he is a poet and it is poetry; and at another time, that he is a soothsayer and it is soothsaying.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti), commentary on Surah 50, verse 6:

﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no fissures?﴾ Did they not look with their eyes, reflecting with their minds, when they denied the resurrection, at the sky existing above them, how We built it without pillars and adorned it with the stars, and it has no cracks (shuquq) that would blemish it?

"And the earth — We spread it out (dahaynaha) over the surface of the water, and We cast into it firm mountains (rawasi), that hold it steady, and We caused to grow in it every kind (zawj) of beautiful (bahij), delightful plant, which gladdens by its beauty."

Note on the passage: ﴿والأَرْض﴾ is in the accusative as a conjunctive (ma'tuf) on the place (mawdi') of ﴿إلى السَّماء﴾ ("to the sky"), i.e., it is governed by the same verb-sense of looking/contemplating in the earlier verse: "...and the earth, how We spread it out..."

Translation of the commentary:

"And the earth" is conjoined (ma'tuf) to the place (mawdi') of "to the sky," as in "how We spread it out" (madadnaha), meaning: We spread it out (dahawnaha) over the surface of the water. "And We cast into it firm mountains" (rawasi), meaning mountains that hold it steady. "And We caused to grow in it every kind (zawj)," meaning every type, "beautiful," meaning it gladdens by its beauty, because of its goodness.

Tabsiratan (insight): an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), meaning We did that as an insight from Us. And a reminder (dhikra): a reminder, for every servant who turns back (munib), returning (raja') to Our obedience.

And We send down from the sky blessed water, abundant in blessing, and therewith We caused to grow gardens (jannat, orchards) and grain (habb al-zar', the seed of crops) that is harvested (al-hasid, the reaped).

﴿And the palm trees, tall (bāsiqāt), having spathes of fruit stacked one above another⟩

Tall: a state (ḥāl) that is anticipated (muqaddarah). ﴿Having spathes of fruit stacked⟩ (ṭalʿ naḍīd): layered, one part of it upon another.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 11:

﴿As a provision for the servants﴾ is a maf'ul lahu (object of purpose). ﴿And We revived thereby a dead land﴾ — it is the same for masculine and feminine. ﴿So too will be the emergence﴾ — i.e., a revival like this one — ﴿the emergence﴾ from the graves. So how can you deny it? The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrir), and the meaning is that they have looked and known what has been mentioned.

Qur'an 50:12: ﴿The people of Noah denied before them﴾. The feminine verb is because of the meaning of "people" (qawm). ﴿And the companions of al-Rass﴾: it is a well, around which they lived with their livestock, worshipping idols; their prophet was, it is said, Handhalah ibn Safwan, and it is said to have been someone else. ﴿And Thamud﴾: the people of Salih.
﴿And ʿĀd﴾ the people of Hūd.

Here is the translation of the passage:

﴿And the companions of al-Ayka﴾ (al-Ayka: a thicket), the people of Shu'ayb, ﴿and the people of Tubba'﴾, who was a king in Yemen. He embraced Islam and invited his people to Islam, but they denied him. ﴿Each﴾ of those mentioned ﴿denied the messengers﴾, like Quraysh, ﴿so My warning was justified﴾, that is, the descent of the punishment became due upon all of them. So do not let your chest be constricted by the disbelief of Quraysh in you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 15:

﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation?﴾ That is: We were not wearied by it, so We shall not be wearied by the re-creation. ﴿Rather, they are in confusion (labs) concerning a new creation﴾ (i.e., doubt) ﴿concerning a new creation﴾, which is the resurrection.

﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know﴾: this is a circumstantial clause (*ḥāl*), with "nahnu" ("We") understood, so it means "and We know." ﴿what﴾ (*mā*) is a verbal-source particle (*maṣdariyya*). ﴿whispers﴾ means speaks within himself (*tuḥaddith*). ﴿with it﴾: the "bi" (بِ) is extra (*zā'ida*), and the pronoun refers to man. ﴿And We are nearer to him﴾ in knowledge ﴿than the jugular vein﴾: the construct (*iḍāfa*) here is explanatory (*lil-bayān*). The *warīdān* are the two veins on either side of the neck.

﴿Idh﴾ (when) is in the accusative case, governed by an implied verb, ﴿اُذْكُرْ﴾ (udhkur, "remember"). ﴿Yatalaqqa﴾ (receives) means takes down and records. ﴿Al-mutalaqqiyan﴾ (the two receivers) are the two angels assigned to the human being to record what he does, ﴿on the right and on the left﴾ of him, ﴿seated﴾, meaning two who are seated. ﴿Qa'id﴾ (seated) is a mubtada' (the subject of a nominal sentence), and its predicate (khabar) is what precedes it.
﴿Not a word does he utter but there is with him a watcher, ready (to record)﴾ [raqīb: a guardian, one who keeps watch; ʿatīd: present, ready]. Each of the two is in the sense of the dual.

And the intoxication of death has come with the truth (ﷻ: ﴿وجاءَتْ سَكْرَة المَوْت﴾) — its overwhelming force and its severity — ﴿بِالحَقِّ﴾, concerning the matter of the Hereafter, so that even the one who denied it sees it plainly, and this is the very severity itself. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾, that is, death, ﴿ما كُنْت مِنهُ تَحِيد﴾: that from which you used to flee and recoil.
And the Trumpet will be blown, for the Resurrection. ﴿That﴾, i.e., the day of the blowing, ﴿is the Day of the Threat﴾ against the disbelievers with the punishment.

And every soul will come, along with it a driver and a witness.

Commentary: "And there came" on that Day "every soul" to the place of gathering, "with it a driver" an angel who drives it to it, "and a witness" who bears witness against it concerning its deeds, and this is the hands and the feet and other than them. And it is said to the disbeliever:

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 50, verse 22:

﴿You were certainly in heedlessness of this﴾ in the world, ﴿which is now befalling you﴾, ﴿so We have removed from you your covering﴾, i.e., We have removed your heedlessness by means of what you now witness, ﴿and your sight today is sharp﴾, i.e., keen, so that you perceive by it what you denied in the world.
﴿And his companion will say﴾, meaning the angel assigned to him, ﴿This is what is with me, ready﴾, meaning present (ḥāḍir). Then it will be said to Malik:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 24:

﴿Cast, both of you, into Hell every stubborn disbeliever﴾. That is: "Cast, cast" (alqi alqi), or "alqiyan" (cast indeed). Al-Hasan recited it thus, and the nun was replaced by an alif, so it became "alqia." ﴿Every stubborn disbeliever﴾ who opposes the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 25:

﴿Withholding from good﴾ such as zakat; ﴿transgressor﴾ wrongdoer; ﴿in doubt﴾ skeptical about his religion.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 26:

﴿Whoever set up another god with Allah⦆ — the subject (mubtada'), whose predicate (khabar) is implicitly understood as a conditional (shart) sense; ﴿then cast him into the severe punishment﴾ — its explanation is similar to what has preceded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 27:

﴿He will say, "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress; rather, he was in far error."﴾ [The companion, i.e., the devil, says:] "Our Lord, I did not make him transgress" (mā aṭghaytuhu), i.e., I did not lead him astray (aḍlaltuhu). "But he was in far error" (wa-lakin kāna fī ḍalāl baʿīd), so I called him and he responded to me. And he [the man] says, "He made me transgress by his calling me to it" (huwa aṭghānī bi-duʿāʾihi lahu).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 28:

﴿He said﴾ (Allah, the Exalted) said: ﴿Do not dispute before Me﴾, i.e., disputing is of no benefit here. ﴿And I had already sent forth to you﴾ in the world ﴿the warning﴾, namely the punishment in the Hereafter, if you did not believe, and it is unavoidable.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 50, verse 29:

﴿The word is not changed with Me﴾ — i.e., it is not altered ﴿regarding that﴾ — ﴿and I am not ever unjust to the servants﴾ — so that I would punish them without any crime. The form ẓallām here means "one who does injustice," in keeping with His saying ﴿There is no injustice today﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 30:

﴿The Day﴾ its governing verb is "Zalla­m" (the one who wrongs, referring to Allah as the one who does not wrong). ﴿We will say﴾ with the nun and with the ya' (both readings). ﴿To Hell: "Are you filled?"﴾ an interrogative for confirmation of His promise to fill it. ﴿And it will say﴾ in the form of a question like a request: ﴿"Is there any more?"﴾ meaning: I do not have room for anything other than what I have been filled with, that is, I have indeed been filled.
﴿And Paradise will be brought near﴾ — brought close — ﴿to the God-fearing﴾ — ﴿in a place not far off﴾ — from them, so that they will see it. And it will be said to them:

﴿This﴾, the one seen, ﴿is what you were promised﴾, read with the ta' and the ya' (تُوعَدُونَ, *tū'adūna* or *yū'adūna*) in the world. The phrase ﴿for every oft-returning one﴾ is in apposition (*badal*, substitution) for ﴿for the God-fearing﴾, and the word قَوْله (*qawluhu*, "his saying") refers to ﴿for every oft-returning one﴾. ﴿Oft-returning﴾ means one who turns back repeatedly to obedience to God, and ﴿watchful﴾ means one who guards His limits.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, "exegesis of the two Jalals") on surah 50, verse 33:**

﴿Whoever feared the Most Merciful unseen﴾ he feared Him while not seeing Him. ﴿And came with a penitent heart﴾ turning toward His obedience. It is also said of the al-Muttaqun (the God-fearing).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 34:

﴿Enter it in peace﴾ (safe from every fear), or with peace; that is, greet one another with peace and enter. ﴿That﴾ is the day on which entry occurs, ﴿the Day of Eternity﴾, the everlasting continuation in the Garden.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 35:

﴿For them there will be whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more.﴾ An increase beyond what they knew and asked for.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 36:

﴿And how many generations We destroyed before them, who were stronger in might than they﴾ That is, We destroyed before the disbelievers of Quraysh many generations of disbelievers, ﴿who were stronger in might﴾ in strength. ﴿And they searched through the lands﴾ they explored them, ﴿Was there any place of escape?﴾ from death for them or for anyone else? ﴿But they found none﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 37:

﴿Indeed, in that﴾ mentioned [matter] ﴿is a reminder﴾ an admonition ﴿for whoever has a heart﴾ meaning, intellect ﴿or gives ear﴾ listens to the admonition ﴿while he is present﴾ attentive with the heart.

﴿And We certainly created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾: the first of them was Sunday and the last was Friday. ﴿And no fatigue touched Us﴾: weariness. It was revealed in refutation of the Jews, who said that God rested on the Sabbath day. The negation of weariness from Him is because He is exalted above the attributes of created beings, and because there is no contact between Him and anything other than Him. ﴿Indeed His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it "Be," and it is.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 39:

﴿So be patient﴾ is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿over what they say﴾, i.e., the Jews and others, of comparisons (tashbih) and denial (takdhib). ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾: pray, praising Him, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, i.e., the dawn prayer (salat al-subh), ﴿and before the setting﴾, i.e., the noon prayer (salat al-zuhr) and the afternoon prayer (salat al-'asr).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 40:

﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾, i.e., pray the two night prayers (al-'ishā'ayn), ﴿and after the prostrations﴾ — with the hamza vowelled with a fatha, it is the plural of dabr (the back/end), and with a kasra it is a verbal noun of adbara (to turn back), meaning: pray the voluntary prayers prescribed (sunan) following the obligatory prayers. It was also said that what is meant is the literal glorification (tasbīh) at these times, accompanied by praise (ḥamd).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 41:

﴿And listen﴾, O you being addressed, to what I say, ﴿on the day when the Caller calls﴾, who is Israfil, ﴿from a place near﴾, near the heaven. It is the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), the closest point on earth to the heaven. He says: O decayed bones, severed joints, torn flesh and scattered hair, indeed Allah commands you to gather together for the judgment of the decision.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 50, verse 42:

﴿The Day﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "the Day" before it. ﴿They will hear﴾, meaning all of creation, ﴿the Cry in truth﴾, meaning the Resurrection. It is the second blast of the Trumpet by Israfil, and it is possible that it occurs both before and after his call. ﴿That﴾, meaning the Day of the call and the hearing, ﴿is the Day of Emergence﴾ from the graves. The verb governing ﴿the Day he calls﴾ is an implied one, meaning: they will know the consequence of their denial.

**﴿On a day﴾** is a *badal* (substitution, a grammatical apposition that replaces the noun it follows) for the **﴿day﴾** before it, and what lies between them is an *i'tiraD* (parenthetical interjection). **﴿The earth will split asunder﴾**: the verb is read with a light shin (*tashaqqa*) or a heavy shin (*tashaqqaqa*), the heavy form arising from the assimilation (*idgham*) of the second *ta'* into the shin, as the original form was *tatashaqqaqu*. **﴿Hastening forth from them﴾**: *sira'an* is the plural of *sari'* (swift), and it is a *hal* (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject) referring to an implied subject, meaning: *fa-yakhrujuna musri'in*, "so they will come out hastening." **﴿That is a gathering, easy for Us﴾**: there is a separation between the qualified noun and its adjective by the element attached to the adjective (*'alayna*, "for Us"), for the sake of *ikhtisas* (specification, emphasising that the matter pertains to Allah alone), and this does no harm. **"That"** refers to the meaning of the gathering that was reported concerning it, namely revival after death, and the assembling for presentation and reckoning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 50, verse 45:

﴿We know best what they say﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Quraysh. ﴿And you are not over them a compeller﴾, forcing them to faith. This was before the command to fight (jihad). ﴿So remind, by the Qur'an, those who fear My warning﴾, and they are the believers.
